newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call money steady, hovers over C.Bank rate.
newsitem.headline: Manila call money steady, hovers over C.Bank rate.

text.p: * Thin turnover prevails over slow session
The Philippine overnight money was unchanged at 10.03125 percent, marginally above the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate, brokers said.
"The market is still very liquid. Lenders are scrambling over each other to lend out money at a very slight premium," one said.
In the absence of borrowers, many lenders had to make do with the Central Bank's 10.0 percent overnight facility to park their excess funds.
Turnover was slight with only 7.517 billion pesos changing hands on rates ranging from 10.03125 percent to 10.25 percent.
Most banks have already squared their weekly reserves position, another trader said, resulting in a quiet session.
The secondary Treasury bill market also slowed down after a slight selling spree of three-month bills after the Central Bank increased its rate to 10.2 percent from 9.9 percent on Wednesday.
Traders said they thought the Central Bank wanted the rates to nudge higher in the coming auctions.
A Reuter poll of six banks showed that secondary market bids for the three-month bills ranged from 10.25 to 10.40 percent.
"There was not much activity in the secondary market today. Everything has settled down from yesterday's brisk trading," a trader said.
